sections.title: Type 1 Conditional (Real Future)
sections.content:
Structure: If + Present Simple, will + base verb. It is used for real and possible situations in the future.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify the if-clause.
Step 2: Check if the situation is real and possible.
Step 3: Use Present Simple in the if-clause.
Step 4: Use will + base verb in the main clause.

Example:
If it rains, we will cancel the match.

sections.title: Type 2 Conditional (Unreal Present)
sections.content:
Structure: If + Simple Past, would + base verb. It expresses imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Check if the situation is imaginary.
Step 2: Use Simple Past in the if-clause.
Step 3: Use would + base verb in the main clause.
Step 4: Use 'were' with all subjects in formal English (If I were...).

Example:
If I were rich, I would buy a house.

sections.title: Type 3 Conditional (Unreal Past)
sections.content:
Structure: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3. It expresses unreal situations in the past.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify if the sentence talks about a past regret or impossible past event.
Step 2: Use had + V3 in the if-clause.
Step 3: Use would have + V3 in the main clause.
Step 4: Ensure both clauses refer to past time.

Example:
If she had studied, she would have passed.

sections.title: Simple Past with Past Perfect
sections.content:
Past Perfect shows the earlier of two past actions. Simple Past shows the later action.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify two past actions.
Step 2: Decide which action happened first.
Step 3: Use Past Perfect (had + V3) for the earlier action.
Step 4: Use Simple Past for the later action.

Example:
She had left before I arrived.

sections.title: Time Clauses (when, before, until, as soon as)
sections.content:
In time clauses referring to the future, we use Present tense, not future tense.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Identify time words (when, before, until, as soon as).
Step 2: Check if the meaning refers to future time.
Step 3: Use Present Simple in the time clause.
Step 4: Use will or other future form in the main clause.

Example:
When she arrives, we will start the meeting.

sections.title: Future Perfect Continuous
sections.content:
Structure: will have been + verb-ing. It shows an action that will continue up to a specific time in the future.

3-4 Step Solution Method:
Step 1: Look for a future time reference (by next year, by 2030).
Step 2: Check if duration is mentioned (for/since).
Step 3: Use will have been + verb-ing.
Step 4: Ensure the action continues up to that future time.

Example:
By next month, she will have been working here for five years.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Using will in the if-clause.
2. Using 'was' instead of 'were' in Type 2.
3. Using future tense in time clauses.
4. Mixing up the order of Past Perfect and Simple Past.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Type 1 = real future possibility. Type 2 = unreal present. Type 3 = unreal past. Earlier past action = Past Perfect. Time clauses use Present tense for future meaning. Future Perfect Continuous shows duration up to a future time.

tricks.title: No Will in If Rule
tricks.explanation: Never use 'will' in the if-clause in standard conditionals.
tricks.example: If he comes, I will help.

tricks.title: Were Trick
tricks.explanation: Use 'were' for all subjects in unreal present situations.
tricks.example: If I were you, I would apologize.

tricks.title: Had + V3 Signal
tricks.explanation: If you see had + V3 in the if-clause, think Type 3 conditional.
tricks.example: If she had called, I would have answered.

tricks.title: Earlier Action Rule
tricks.explanation: The action that happened first in the past takes Past Perfect.
tricks.example: He had finished the work before he left.

tricks.title: Time Clause Present Rule
tricks.explanation: After when, before, until, as soon as, use Present tense for future meaning.
tricks.example: As soon as he finishes, he will call me.

tricks.title: Future Duration Clue
tricks.explanation: If you see 'by + future time' and duration, think Future Perfect Continuous.
tricks.example: By 2027, she will have been teaching for ten years.

tricks.title: Would Have Clue
tricks.explanation: Would have + V3 indicates unreal past result.
tricks.example: She would have won if she had tried.

tricks.title: Avoid Double Future
tricks.explanation: Do not use future tense in both clauses of a time sentence.
tricks.example: When he arrives, we will begin.
